SMTO-UI-0001 — Browser request failed

GUID: 188f9539-e772-4226-957f-28e277a1f788
Slug: ui-network-failed
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Your browser couldn't reach the SMTO server, so the page got no reply. If you were saving or sending something, it may or may not have reached SMTO.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure your computer is connected to the network and that the computer running the SMTO server is switched on. The page has to reach the server to load or save anything.
  2. Once you're connected, reload the page. Reloading shows what the server has saved right now.
  3. Check whether your action already happened: open the task, conversation or setting and look for your change before doing it again. The server may have done it even though the reply never arrived, and repeating it could do it twice.

What success looks like

  • The page loads current information, and you can see whether your earlier action happened.

If it still fails

  • If the page won't load at all, select Copy error details (if you still can) and tell the person who manages SMTO that the server can't be reached. Don't assume an action failed just because the connection dropped.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser could not complete a service request or load the requested state.

What this means

  • The browser fetch wrapper catches a transport exception, and some UI paths also classify failed settings or state loads under this broad family. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The browser fetch wrapper catches a transport exception, and some UI paths also classify failed settings or state loads under this broad family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether fetch failed or the service returned an unsuccessful response; do not assume the server is offline.

How to fix it

  • SMTOErrors.fetch caught a fetch() rejection before any HTTP response (network down, Server unreachable or stopped, proxy or TLS reset), or a UI script failed to load; for writes the outcome is marked unknown. Confirm the Server is running and reachable at this page's address, then re-read the current state (run, conversation or setting) to establish whether the write took effect before resubmitting.
  • Check browser connectivity and the recorded service response, then refresh authoritative state before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The current state loads successfully and any earlier mutation is reconciled before resubmission.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
